# 1 Enoch Chapter 88 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 88 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 88:2 — 'blind sheep' — who are these?

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those-blind-sheep" | Literal; 'blind' modifies 'sheep' — these are sheep who cannot see |
| LOGOS | "those blind sheep" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the blind sheep [the fallen Watchers who had become like sheep]" | Adds interpretation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text. The 'blind sheep' is one of the most textually difficult terms in this passage. They are distinct from the regular sheep (the elect). Most commentators identify them with the fallen Watchers who have taken on the 'sheep' (animal/human) form. 'Blind' suggests spiritual blindness — they could not see their own guilt. The interpretation is placed in the SOPHIA notes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Clean text; interpretation in notes.

---

## 88:1 — 'he gave me a sword' — significance

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he-gave-me-a-sword" | Literal; the sword is not further described |
| LOGOS | "he gave me a sword" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "He handed me a sword" | Minor variation; 'handed' for 'gave' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three converge on the basic act. 'Gave' (LOGOS/EMET) is adopted. The sword's meaning is discussed in notes — it may represent Enoch's role as a witness who participates in the judgment, or simply his protection as an observer.

**Status:** Converged on basic act.

---

## 88:3 — 'to the right of that house'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-the-right-of-that-house" | Literal; spatial location relative to the heavenly dwelling |
| LOGOS | "to the right of that house" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "to the right of that house [the heavenly dwelling]" | Adds identification |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS clean text. The identification ('heavenly dwelling') is placed in SOPHIA notes. The spatial detail is significant: the judgment-place is literally adjacent to the divine throne room — this reflects the architecture of 1 Enoch's heaven (cf. ch. 14).

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
